title: How a Spark Plug Lights Your Engine

sections.name: How a Spark Plug Lights Your Engine

lines.label: hook
lines.head: *20,000 volts*, thousands of times a minute

lines: Your car turns twelve volts into a spark of over twenty thousand volts, thousands of times a minute.
The battery supplies about twelve volts. Far too weak to jump a gap on its own.

prop.sub: WHAT THE COIL MAKES FROM 12 VOLTS

lines: An ignition coil uses two windings of wire to step that up to tens of thousands of volts, in an instant.
At the tip of the plug, the voltage jumps a gap of about a millimetre, lighting the fuel and air.
The engine computer fires each plug just before the piston reaches the top, so the burn pushes at exactly the right time.
Over time the tips wear and the gap grows. You get rough idling, hard starts, and worse fuel economy.
Many plugs last tens of thousands of miles, long life iridium ones much longer. Your service book has the exact interval.
Twelve volts in, twenty thousand out, one tiny spark at a time.
